title: Development of a Microphysiological Cartilage‐on‐Chip Platform for Biomechanical Stimulation
author: Peitso, Sarmadian, et al.
materials: This protocol outlines the procedure for preparing the chiron's cartilage‐on‐chip device for RNA extraction. RNA extraction process using an RNA kit is not described in this protocol. Depending on the number of cells inside the cartilage‐on‐chip or the type of hydrogel used, different RNA kits can be preferred. For agarose hydrogel the RNeasy micro kit (Qiagen, cat. no. 74004) is recommended. Always take the RNA dissociation buffer from the kit that will be used for the RNA extraction assay. Using the recommended kit, the expected RNA yield is 200 ng/chip from a single agarose hydrogel.

steps.title: Select RNA extraction kit
steps.instruction: Choose the RNeasy micro kit (Qiagen, cat. no. 74004) for agarose hydrogel samples and note that the expected RNA yield is 200 ng per chip.

steps.title: Prepare low‑melting agarose
steps.instruction: Microwave low‑melting agarose (first test your microwave to determine the required time), then place the melted agarose in a water bath for at least 10 min at 57 °C to ensure uniform dissolution; afterwards cool the agarose to 37 °C before mixing with chondrocytes.

substeps.instruction: Test microwave heating time and adjust as needed.
Keep agarose in water bath ≥10 min at 57 °C.
Cool agarose to 37 °C before cell addition.

steps.title: Wash chondrocytes and add trypsin
steps.instruction: Wash chondrocytes with PBS, then add warm trypsin to maximize enzymatic activity before mixing with the cooled agarose.

steps.title: Prepare agarose‑cell mixture
steps.instruction: Make a PBS‑agarose solution at 4 % (w/v); mix this 1:1 with the cell suspension (3 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹) to obtain a final solution of 2 % (w/v) agarose and 1.5 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹. If the cell suspension is up to 50 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹ (equivalent to 25 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹ in the model), adjust accordingly. Perform the mixing on an Eppendorf heating block to avoid premature gelation.

substeps.instruction: Mix 1:1 with cell suspension (3 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹) → final 2 % agarose, 1.5 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹.
If using higher cell densities (up to 50 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹), adjust mixing to achieve 25 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹ in the model.
Use an Eppendorf heating block for mixing.

steps.title: Inject mixture into chip
steps.instruction: Load the prepared cell‑agarose solution into each cartilage‑on‑chip device; the entire injection protocol may take up to 3 h depending on the number of devices.

steps.title: Perform medium change
steps.instruction: Replace the culture medium every 48–72 h; each medium‑change step typically requires about 30 min.

steps.title: Actuate cartilage‑on‑chip
steps.instruction: Carry out preparation, mechanical actuation, and a medium change together; the combined procedure takes approximately 1–2 h and should be performed at the same time each day for consistency.

steps.title: Remove agarose hydrogel and fix tissue
steps.instruction: If removal is required, the hydrogel removal protocol can take up to 2 h; subsequent fixation (including incubation and washing) generally requires 1–2 h.

steps.title: Extract RNA from chip
steps.instruction: Rinse cells on the chip with PBS, pipetting up and down 10 times; lyse cells with the RNA dissociation buffer from the selected kit, pipetting up and down 20 times (excessive pressure is acceptable). If extraction is not continued immediately, store samples at –80 °C. Allocate roughly 1 h for the RNA dissociation step.

substeps.instruction: Lyse with RNA dissociation buffer – pipette up/down 20× (use strong pressure).
